title: Modeling Shipping Emissions: Machine Learning, Engineering, and Policy Counterfactuals
abstract: arXiv:2610.01008v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Machine learning predicts outcomes well, but predictive accuracy does not ensure reliable counterfactual responses. We examine how to combine machine learning and theory for measurement and counterfactual analysis, using maritime CO2 emissions where physics provides a benchmark speed response. Matching hourly tracking data for dry bulk and container ships to annual fuel consumption reported under EU regulations, we compare engineering calculations, structural regressions, hybrid models, and machine learning. Out of sample, all estimated models predict within a few percent of reported totals, outperforming standard engineering calculations. Yet pure machine learning and unrestricted structural regression imply attenuated speed responses. Hybrids preserve the structural component's speed response by excluding speed-related inputs from the machine learning component. A cost-benefit analysis of speed reductions illustrates the policy stakes:

translated_title: 航运排放建模：机器学习、工程方法与政策反事实分析
translated_abstract: 机器学习能够很好地预测结果，但预测的准确性并不能保证可靠的反事实响应。我们研究了如何将机器学习与理论相结合以进行测量和反事实分析，并以海上二氧化碳排放为研究对象，因为物理学为此提供了一个基准的速度响应。我们将干散货船和集装箱船的逐小时追踪数据与欧盟法规下报告的年度燃料消耗量相匹配，比较了工程计算、结构回归、混合模型和机器学习方法。在样本外，所有估计模型的预测结果与报告总量的偏差都在几个百分点以内，优于标准的工程计算。然而，纯机器学习和无约束的结构回归会导致速度响应被衰减。混合模型通过在机器学习部分中排除与速度相关的输入，从而保留了结构部分的速度响应。对船舶减速航行的成本效益分析说明了政策利害关系所在。
tldr: 该论文提出一种混合建模方法，将机器学习的预测能力与物理/结构模型的速度响应相结合，从而能够可靠地评估航运减排政策（如船舶减速）的反事实效果。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a hybrid modeling approach that combines machine learning's predictive accuracy with physics-based structural speed responses, enabling reliable counterfactual policy analysis for maritime CO2 emission reductions.
